2. Heard learned Senior Counsel Mr.R R Marshal with Mr.Kunal Shah, learned Advocate for the applicant and learned Advocate Mr.Prem Dave appearing for the org. complainant and learned APP,

sentences.text: Mr.Manan Mehta for respondent - State.

3. Learned Senior Counsel Mr.Marshal upon instructions states that dispute between the parties is amicably settled and the complainant does not have any objection if the applicant is released on anticipatory bail.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/12235/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined

4. The aforesaid statement made by learned Senior Counsel Mr.Marshal was not disputed by the learned Advocate Mr.Dave and Mr.Dave has placed on record the affidavit of the org. complainant which reads thus:
"Affidavit of Dhaval Hasmukhbhai Mehta -Org.

Complainant"
I, Dhaval Hasmukhbhai Mehta, aged 42, residing at; 47, Seems Row House, b/h Shiv Shakti Sweets,
Ghoddod Road, Surat, original complainant of the present FIR, do solemnly affirm and state on oath as under:-
1. I state that I am the victim/original complainant in connection with the FIR No.11210069230440 of 2023 registered with Althan Police Station, Surat u/s. 420,
120(b), 409 of the Indian Penal Code.

(Section 409 was added during the investigation.)
2.

I say that since the disputes between us out of which the criminal proceeding has arisen have been compromised between the parties; upon the intervention of the family members and other senior members of community and area.
Problems and errors related to the dispute have been solved.
We have settled the disputes and misunderstandings amicably and in mindful manner.
Therefore, continuing with the present proceedings of the anticipatory bail in connection with the said FIR would only amount to misuse of the process of Court."

3. I state that in view of what is stated herein above I do not object to the granting of anticipatory bail to the present applicant Mr.Yogesh Khemchand Agraval in which he has preferred before this Hon'ble Court in connection with the FIR No.11210069230440 of 2023 registered with Althan Police Station, Surat u/s. 420, 120(b), 409 of the Indian Penal Code.
(Section 409 was added during the investigation.)
I jointly pray to allow the petition and grant the relief as prayed for in the the present application."
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/12235/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined 5.

By placing the aforesaid affidavit on record, both the learned Counsels have jointly submitted that the present applicant be granted anticipatory bail and Mr.Dave states that he does not have any objection if the anticipatory bail is granted to the applicant in view of the fact that the dispute is Yogesh Khemchand Agraval vs State Of Gujarat on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61287480/
2 settled between the parties.

sentences.text:
6. In view of the aforesaid consensus arrived at between the parties which has not been disputed by the learned APP Mr.Mehta upon instructions, no further reasons required to be given and without discussing the evidence in detail, at this stage, I am inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
7. This Court has considered following aspects:

( a) The affidavit filed by Mr.Dave appearing for the org.
complainant dated 18/07/2023 which is already referred to herein above indicates that the dispute is settled between the parties.
(b) The applicant has shown willingness to co-operate with the investigation.
(c) No antecedent is found as submitted by learned Advocate for the applicant.
8. In the facts and circumstances of the present case, since the custodial interrogation of the applicant is not required, I am inclined to consider the case of the applicant.

9. This Court has also taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre Vs. State of Maharashtra and Ors., reported NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/12235/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined at [2011] 1 SCC 694,
wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court reiterated the law laid down by the Constitution Bench in the case of Shri Gurubaksh Singh Sibbia & Ors. Vs. State of Punjab, reported at (1980) 2 SCC 565.
10.

sentences.text: 11. Despite this order, it would be open for the Investigating Agency to apply to the competent Magistrate, for police remand of the applicant.

The applicant shall remain present before the learned Magistrate on the first date of hearing of such application and on all subsequent occasions,
as may be directed by the learned Magistrate.
This would be sufficient to treat the accused in the judicial custody for the purpose of entertaining application of the prosecution for police remand.

This is, however, without prejudice to the right of the accused to seek stay against an order of remand, if, ultimately, granted, and the power of the learned Magistrate to consider such a request in accordance with law.

It is clarified that the applicant, even if, remanded to the police custody,
upon completion of such period of police remand, shall be set free immediately, subject to other conditions of this anticipatory bail order.
12. At the trial, the concerned trial court shall not be influenced by the prima facie observations made by this Court in the present order.
